title: Guard spec v1 — status
description: The single machine-readable answer to 'where is this project and what should happen next'. Every human rendering (CLI text, agent brief, skill instructions) derives from this document so they cannot disagree. Computed from the claims file, the evidence, the baseline and the current working tree; never from a cached verdict alone.

state.description: no-claims: no claims file. unclaimed-changes: the change measured against a reference touches source files that carry no claim and no excusing ignore entry (only computed when a reference is known; it precedes every evidence state because the claim is written before more code). unprobed: claims but no confirmed evidence. evidence-stale: evidence exists but a claim, fault, target or defender changed since. provisional-only: only sub-N evidence exists. unproven: current evidence has findings not covered by the baseline. clean: every finding is killed or baselined.

next.description: The one action that moves the project forward. `command` is a shell line when the action is a tool command, or an instruction when it is not (write-test, claim for a test file).

file.description: For claim (and for scaffold when a change is known): the first uncovered changed file the action is about.

target.description: For write-test / review-fault-change: the finding the action is about.

flakyDefenderSets.description: Distinct defender sets that failed at least once on unmodified source.

worstFlakeRate.description: Highest observed failures/runs on unmodified source across all records, 0–1. A number, so "unstable" stops being an adjective.

stale.description: Why the evidence no longer describes the working tree. Empty when it does.

changedFaults.description: Faults whose find/replace content differs from what the evidence probed. A changed fault that previously survived is the cheapest way to make a finding disappear without a test; it is surfaced, never hidden.

findings.description: Unproven findings from the current evidence, ranked, new first, capped.

changes.description: Claim coverage of the change since `ref`, present only when a reference was given (--changed) or detected from CI. Uncovered files come first in every rendering: the claim is written before more code. Same per-file shapes as the gate document.
